{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA; alternatively, arcsine transformation for proportion analysis if treating as continuous",
    "Given the large sample size (n=76655), check for violations of homogeneity of variance using Levene's test; if violated, use Welch's ANOVA",
    "Check for extreme outliers in Path Efficiency (max=29.817, mean=0.475, sd=0.467) which may indicate right-skew or recording errors",
    "Consider mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect to account for repeated measures across 8 mice"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For significant ANOVA results, perform Tukey's HSD for all pairwise comparisons among the 5 stimulation paradigms",
    "For Welch's ANOVA, use Games-Howell post-hoc test",
    "For logistic regression on Success, use estimated marginal means with pairwise comparisons on log-odds scale",
    "Focus comparisons on Sham vs. active stimulation conditions, and Combined vs. unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only)",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d or eta-squared) for all pairwise comparisons"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all tests within each response variable; for familywise error across all 5 response variables, use Bonferroni adjustment (alpha = 0.01) or control FDR across the entire analysis family",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Stimulation paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels, making ordinal regression inappropriate. Recommend: (1) Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response and the 5 performance variables as predictors—this directly models paradigm classification from behavior; (2) Alternatively, random forest or gradient boosting classifier (XGBoost/LightGBM) to capture non-linear interactions between performance variables, with Mouse held out for cross-validation to assess generalization; (3) Given class imbalance (Combined=63.7%, Sham=4.6%), use stratified sampling, class weights, or SMOTE; (4) Evaluate with balanced accuracy, macro-F1, and confusion matrix rather than raw accuracy; (5) Feature importance analysis to identify which performance variables most discriminate paradigms",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals; given n=76655, central limit theorem applies but check for extreme skew in Path Efficiency",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equal variances across paradigms; likely violated given Sham SD likely differs from Combined",
    "Independence: Assess autocorrelation in repeated measures; use mixed models or cluster-robust SEs if Mouse effects present",
    "Multicollinearity: Check correlations among Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD (likely high); consider PCA or ridge regularization for predictive models",
    "Outliers: Examine extreme values in Path Efficiency (max=29.8) and Time-to-Target (max=201.4) for data quality issues",
    "Complete separation check in logistic models for Success (Sham mean=0.27, Combined=0.78, no complete separation expected)"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham will show significantly lower Success, higher Time-to-Target, lower Path Efficiency, lower Average Speed, and lower AD compared to all active stimulation paradigms",
    "Combined stimulation will outperform unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) on Success and Time-to-Target, consistent with sensory enhancement effects",
    "Bright Visual Only will outperform Dim Visual Only on Success and Path Efficiency, reflecting visual salience effects",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will be highest in Combined and Bright Visual Only conditions, suggesting more exploratory or distributed search patterns with stronger sensory input",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only will show intermediate performance, potentially non-distinguishable from each other",
    "Predictive model will achieve highest classification accuracy for Sham vs. active conditions, with difficulty discriminating among unimodal active conditions"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Cross-sectional design with unbalanced group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs. Sham n=3505) reduces power for Sham comparisons and may inflate Type I error for rare paradigms",
    "No trial-level temporal information (learning effects, fatigue) available in current data view",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (0.0009 to 29.8) suggesting possible calculation artifacts or outliers that may distort parametric analyses",
    "Single replication (Run 26, Replication 1) prevents assessment of reproducibility; between-run variance unknown",
    "Mouse-level clustering (8 mice) with unequal observations per mouse (SC21LM=10986 vs. SC11LM=7233) may confound stimulation effects with individual differences",
    "AD interpretation as 'angular dispersion' is assumed from abbreviation; without ground truth, directional vs. spatial dispersion ambiguity remains",
    "Temperature=0.5 for LLM generation may produce variable outputs; deterministic analysis preferred for replication",
    "No information on trial randomization, counterbalancing, or stimulus parameters (ICMS intensity, visual luminance values)"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response, all five performance variables as fixed effects, and Mouse as random intercept; compare to random forest classifier with 5-fold stratified cross-validation; report confusion matrix, per-class precision/recall, and SHAP values for feature interpretation; additionally, conduct equivalence testing (TOST) to determine if ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only are statistically equivalent rather than just non-significantly different"
}
